A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GMLLM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite retitling and extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments, explanation-quality evaluations, token and runtime measurements, ablations, and a human evaluation study.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds MalGuard comparisons and experiments with Qwen3.5-Flash and DeepSeek-V3.2.

M1.justification: Equation 5 changes the stated mask-optimization loss from log(1-p) to -log(p+epsilon), where p is the malicious-class probability. The graph construction, GNN architecture, rule features, and LLM pipeline remain stable. Budgeted top-K extraction was already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Python package detection and behavior descriptions using Backstabbers, Datadog, Mal-OSS, and MalCP. The new backbone experiment samples existing MalCP coverage; it introduces no new dataset, population, domain, or task.

E2.justification: v3 adds MalGuard to Tables 1–2 and direct-prompting Qwen3.5-Flash and DeepSeek-V3.2 comparators in Appendix E.2. The existing comparator sets are retained, making this a targeted extension.

E3.justification: The stated evaluation design changes materially: v1 describes a fixed-seed split and permits early stopping on test F1; v3 specifies independently repeated splits and reserves test data exclusively for evaluation (D.2.1–D.2.3). New Appendix E.2 also introduces a stratified 600-package evaluation with recall and F1 reporting. These are documented protocol changes, without establishing that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.2 tests whether detection and token-efficiency benefits depend on the original LLM backbones. The rule/component ablations, K sensitivity analysis, attention visualizations, and five qualitative cases were already present and remain substantively unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions already report averages over five trials. v3 explicitly specifies five independent seeds for splitting and training, revising v1's fixed-seed split description. The human-study sample size and Spearman correlation reporting remain unchanged; changed correlation values do not establish a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds MalGuard results and backbone detection/token results in Tables 11–12. Table 7 revises correlations and p-values, including human–human Threat Generalization correlation from 0.613 to 0.630. Existing detection, explanation, token, ablation, and runtime entries otherwise remain unchanged. The additional backbone results are new comparisons, not demonstrated v1-to-v3 performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 11 changes the selection inequalities from below-threshold to above-threshold attention, correcting their inconsistency with v1's prose. Equation 5 also revises the formal loss definition. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: graph-guided localization improves LLM-based malicious Python package detection while reducing irrelevant context and resource use. Retitling and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning backbone independence, predictable token costs, and preservation of performance on small packages. Its new Impact Statement discusses developer harm from false positives, adversarial exploitation of explanations, and the intended role of human oversight.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a concrete code-repository link, explicit deduplication and split-construction instructions, and tokenizer/input-accounting details in D.3. These supplement the extensive implementation documentation already in v1; newly described preprocessing does not itself establish that preprocessing changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to MalGuard by Gao et al. (2025) and Wei et al. (2024). The broader survey and Appendix B's positioning against code-embedding and dynamic-analysis methods remain substantially unchanged. Citation-style and bibliographic updates are primarily editorial.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title, GMLLM's expanded name, abstract opening, and selected experimental explanations; fixes unresolved author citations; and adds impact, acknowledgment, and appendix subsections. Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references move from one-column to two-column formatting, substantially changing figure and table placement and sizing. Figure 1's panels become vertically stacked, Tables 1–3 share a page, and appendix visualizations occupy separate pages. Tables 11–12 are added, while existing graph figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical consistency, adds useful comparator and backbone evidence, and makes data handling, token accounting, and code access clearer. These are meaningful but limited gains. Although the revised protocol excludes test-based stopping, the PDFs do not connect that revision to reruns of the unchanged main results, so a substantial improvement in empirical validity is not established.
